templates.text: A sudden shadow passes overhead → eyes track sluggishly for a moment, then gaze drifts away.
Bright light from a window → a slow, partial blink, followed by a faint, delayed grimace.
A red ball moves slowly → a weak, uncoordinated reach begins but falters before completion.
A nurse's face enters the visual field → a brief, quiet stare, then the head lolls to the side.
Ceiling fan blades turning → eyes follow one rotation, then lose focus and become glassy.
A mobile sways gently → a soft, intermittent coo, then the eyes close as if overwhelmed.
A camera flash → a delayed startle with only a slight jerk of the arms, no full Moro.
A patterned blanket is shifted → visual fixation breaks after {seconds} seconds with a sigh.
A hand waves near the face → a slow, incomplete attempt to turn the head toward the motion.
Sunlight glints off a monitor → squinting occurs, but the head does not turn to avoid the glare.
A black-and-white contrast card is presented → a weak, fleeting alertness that quickly dissolves.
A slow-moving toy → eyes attempt pursuit but lag behind, resulting in a jerky, broken track.
Overhead lights are dimmed → pupils dilate slowly, with a delayed, shallow sigh of relief.
A face leans in close → a brief, quiet visual lock, then the eyes wander without social smiling.
A curtain is drawn open → a slow blink sequence, followed by a faint, abortive limb movement.
A spinning rattle → a weak orienting response that ends in a yawn and gaze aversion.
A sudden change in ambient light → a sluggish pupillary reflex, with minimal behavioral change.
A large, slow-moving object → a fragmented attempt at visual following, soon abandoned.
A soft light is turned on → eyes open partially, then close again after a few shallow breaths.
A caregiver's moving finger → a delayed saccade attempts to catch up, but coordination is poor.
Shadows play on the wall → a quiet, disorganized staring, lacking sustained attention.
A colorful blanket is lifted → a faint increase in alertness that fades within moments.
A slow horizontal sweep of a penlight → tracking is attempted but is incomplete and arrhythmic.
A sudden visual expansion (like an opening umbrella at a distance) → a muted, partial startle.
A high-contrast edge is introduced → fixation is brief and unstable, followed by eye rubbing.
A gentle rocking motion in view → visual interest is shown but without coordinated head movement.
A change from dark to moderately lit room → pupils adjust slowly, with a delayed whimper.
A large, static geometric shape → a short period of looking, then a lapse into drowsy inactivity.
A reflective surface glimmers → a weak orienting turn of the head that stops halfway.
A slow, predictable visual pattern → a drowsy, intermittent attention that fails to sustain.
